title: Interview Transcription App: Record, Transcribe, Get Notes
description: Record an interview on your phone and get a transcript plus notes with each question and answer, quotes and follow-ups. Built-in apps and Cassette.
h1: An interview transcription app that writes the notes too
answer: Your phone can already record and transcribe an interview: Voice Memos shows a transcript on iPhone 12 or later in the languages Apple supports, the Recorder app does it on Pixel phones, and Voice Recorder on Galaxy phones with Galaxy AI can transcribe a recording. What they leave to you is the write-up. Cassette records the interview, writes the transcript, and for an interview in English it writes interview notes too: the context, each main question with a short summary of the answer, the most telling quotes, the facts stated and the follow-ups promised.

sections.h: Before you start: get a recording you can transcribe

blocks.p: A transcript is only as good as the sound. A few small things make the difference.

ul: **Ask first.** Tell the person you are recording and why, before you press record.
**Put the phone between you,** flat on the table, closer to the person you are interviewing than to you. Their answers matter more than your questions.
**Pick a quiet room.** A cafe's music and cups end up in the transcript as gaps and wrong words.
**Silence the phone.** Turn on Do Not Disturb so a buzz doesn't cover an answer.
**Check battery and storage** before a long conversation.

sections.h: Transcribe an interview with the app your phone came with

blocks.p: If a transcript is all you need, start here. It costs nothing.

**On iPhone,** record in Voice Memos. On iPhone 12 or later you can [view a transcript](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/view-a-transcription-iph00953a982/ios) of the recording in the languages Apple supports, and copy it out.

**On a Pixel,** the Recorder app writes a live transcript as you record. Google's page on [transcriptions](https://support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/16267698?hl=en) lists the languages for each Pixel and says Pixel 8 and later can also summarize a recording of 5 minutes to an hour.

**On a Galaxy phone,** Voice Recorder has an **Interview** mode that records sound from the top and bottom of the phone, so you can lay it between two people. On phones with Galaxy AI it can also [transcribe and summarize](https://www.samsung.com/us/support/answer/ANS10000942/) the recording.
Either way you end up with a long block of text. Pulling out what each answer said, the lines worth quoting and what you promised to send is still your job.
Cassette looks like a tape deck and works like one. It runs on iPhone and Android, and the steps are the same on both.

ol: **Press RECORD.** The tape keeps rolling when the screen locks, so you can put the phone down and look at the person, not the screen.
**Tap MARK** when an answer is one you will want again. The mark holds that moment on the tape.
**Press STOP** at the end. Cassette writes the transcript and the notes, with no outside AI service.

Cassette recording on an Android phone, with the same deck.

blocks.p: Interviewing someone over a video call? On a Mac, set Cassette's switch to **CALL** and it records the call's sound together with your microphone, with nothing joining the call. The [Zoom on Mac guide](/cassette/guides/record-zoom-meeting-on-mac/) has the steps.

sections.h: What the interview notes look like

blocks.p: Cassette picks the kind of notes from what it hears. For an interview in English it writes:

ul: The **context**: who and what, only as said.
Each main **question** asked, with a one or two sentence summary of the **answer**.
The most telling **quotes**, in the person's own words.
The **facts** stated: names, numbers and dates.
The **follow-ups**: what either of you promised to send or do.

alts: Interview notes in Cassette on iPhone, with quotes and a question with its answer.
Interview notes in Cassette on Android, with quotes and a question with its answer.

blocks.p: The notes report what was said. Cassette is told never to judge, score or rate the person, which matters for a job interview.

If it guessed wrong, for example an interview it took for a meeting, choose **Interview** from the notes type list and the notes are written again. These interview notes are for tapes in English. An interview in another language still gets its transcript and general notes, without this layout.

The notes type list in Cassette on Android, with Interview picked.

blocks.p: On an iPhone without Apple Intelligence or on a version before iOS 26, or an Android phone with less than 8 GB of memory, you get the recording, the transcript and a few lines heard clearly, word for word, instead of these notes.

On iPhone, iPad and Mac, Cassette can bring in an audio file you already have: share it to Cassette on iPhone or iPad, press **ADD FILE** on the Shelf, or drag it onto the Shelf on a Mac. A long recording dragged straight from Voice Memos on a Mac has to go to the Desktop first. Cassette reads M4A, MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC, Opus and the sound in an MP4. The file becomes a tape with a transcript and notes under the same free tape rule, and the original isn't changed.

ul: **Read the transcript.** Open the tape and tap TRANSCRIPT for the whole conversation as text.
**Keep the notes with your others.** Send them to Notion, OneNote, Evernote or Google Keep, to Apple Notes on iPhone, or to Samsung Notes on a Samsung phone.
**Ask your tapes.** On a phone that writes full notes, type a question like "what did she say about pricing?" and get an answer from your own recordings.

faq.q: Is there a free interview transcription app?
faq.a: Yes. Voice Memos on iPhone, Recorder on Pixel phones and Voice Recorder on Galaxy phones with Galaxy AI can all transcribe for free. Cassette records for free with no time limit. A tape under {short_tape_minutes} minutes is transcribed free, and {free_tapes} longer tapes a month are too. Most interviews are longer, and Premium covers every tape after that.

faq.q: Does it work without the internet?
faq.a: On Android, the phone writes the transcript itself, and the notes model arrives over Wi-Fi once after you install, so open Cassette on Wi-Fi before you need it. On iPhone, the transcript is written on the device in the languages it supports there, once that language's speech model is downloaded. Otherwise Apple's servers write it.

faq.q: Can I keep the interview private?
faq.a: Notes are never written by an outside AI service. On Android, the audio only leaves the phone if you sign in with Premium, which backs tapes up. On iPhone there are more cases: Apple's servers transcribe a tape the phone can't do on the device, the notes can be written on Apple's Private Cloud Compute on iOS 27, and tapes go in iCloud and computer backups and in your Premium backup. To stop all of that, turn on On-device only in your Cassette profile.

faq.q: Will the person know they are being recorded?
faq.a: Cassette doesn't tell them, so tell them yourself before you press RECORD.
